Hi Sophie — looping in a few technical details you asked about so the deep-dive is efficient. Short answers up front: yes, we compared Bedrock, Vertex, and Anthropic; results in the attached playbook.

Notes: 
- Quantization: for the family you described we see 8-bit quantization generally preserves >98% of rerank NDCG for our workload and reduces inference latency by ~25% vs FP16 in our benchmarks; 4-bit gives larger gains but varies by model topology. We include kernel selection and compilation notes in the playbook.
- Observability/tracing: Redwood emits OpenTelemetry spans and we provide a request_id per inference call that is included in the span and in the per-request cost log (token counts, batching breakdown). You can pipe spans to Datadog; we have a prebuilt exporter and example dashboard.
- Dashboards: per-route QPS/latency, per-model token-cost waterfall, KV cache hit-rate, and trace-linked error diagnostics. 

Attached: observability-playbook-20260213.pdf (playbook + example dashboards).

For the deep-dive I'd propose this agenda: 1) Topology & model variants used in tests (15m), 2) Live walkthrough of OpenTelemetry traces + Datadog dashboard (25m), 3) Load test plan + canary/fallback demo (15m), 4) Q&A and next steps (5m).

Marissa — I can host the demo and bring one of the engineers who owns the tracing export.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
